transcript.content: Hi, I’m glad you came in. What brings you in today?

I came in because I was working on a memorial piece for my aunt, and I kept having these awful thoughts that I was going to dishonor her somehow. Like if I put one photo in the wrong place or chose the wrong color, it meant I didn’t love her enough. I couldn’t just let it go like normal creative doubt.
When those thoughts came up, did you feel driven to keep rearranging or rechecking the memorial to make sure it was exactly right?

Yes. I’d reread the label text, nudge the same objects around, and keep checking photos of the layout until it felt settled. Part of me knows it’s already fine, but I still lose a lot of studio time doing it.
Do these thoughts feel intrusive and unwanted to you?
Yes. They feel really unwanted. I don’t want to think that a color choice or where I put a photo means I didn’t love my aunt enough, but the thought keeps coming back and I can’t just brush it off.
On days when this is happening, do these thoughts and the checking take up more than an hour of your day?

Yes, sometimes it does. I’ll spend a long time rereading the labels, moving things slightly, and checking the layout photos until it feels settled. I know it’s probably fine, but it can take up a lot of my studio time.
Do you get these kinds of intrusive doubts and repeated checking in other parts of your life besides this memorial?

Mostly it’s around this. I get stuck rereading the labels, adjusting the same objects, and checking the layout photos again and again until it feels settled, even though I know it’s probably already fine.
Since your aunt died, have you been having a lot of yearning or longing for her?
I’m not sure I’d call it a lot of yearning. I miss her, of course, but it’s more that I get caught up in making sure the memorial is right.
Before your aunt died, did you ever have similar intrusive doubts that led you to recheck or rearrange things repeatedly?

Not really, no. This started around the memorial. I’ll reread the label text, nudge the same objects, and keep checking the layout photos until it feels settled, even though I know it’s probably already fine.
Have these thoughts and checking been interfering with your work or daily life?
I’m still getting most of my work done, but it’s taking extra time in the studio. I already missed a grant deadline because of it, and I backed out of a gallery talk I’d actually wanted to do.
Do you think these thoughts and checking will stop once the memorial is finished?

I don’t know. I keep thinking that once it’s finished I should be able to let it go, but the thoughts feel bigger than just normal creative doubts. It’s this awful feeling that if I place something wrong or choose the wrong color, I’m dishonoring her—like it means I didn’t love her enough. I can’t just brush that off.
Outside of the memorial, have you been worrying a lot about other parts of your life?
I’m not sure. I haven’t really noticed it spreading to other parts of my life in the same way. It mostly feels tied to the memorial.
Since your aunt died, do you find yourself preoccupied with thoughts about her for much of the day?
I’m not sure I’d say it’s for much of the day. I do think about her when I’m working on the memorial, obviously, but outside of that I haven’t really noticed myself being preoccupied with it all day.
Since your aunt died, have you been feeling intense sadness?
I don’t know if I’d call it intense sadness. I’ve felt upset at times, but it hasn’t felt overwhelming all the time.
Since your aunt died, have you been having trouble accepting that she’s gone?
I mean, I know she’s gone. It’s painful, but I haven’t felt like I can’t accept it.
Do you feel that your fear of dishonoring your aunt by placing something wrong is excessive or doesn’t really make sense, even while it still feels hard to shake?

Yes, I think part of me knows it’s excessive. It’s just a memorial piece, and normally I could make choices and move on. But I kept having these unwanted thoughts that if I put one photo in the wrong place or chose the wrong color, it meant I didn’t love her enough or was dishonoring her. I couldn’t shake it.
Do these thoughts and the checking happen only when you’re working on the memorial?

Mostly when I’m working on it. I’ll reread the label text, keep nudging the same objects, and look at the layout photos over and over until it feels settled. I know it’s already fine, but I end up losing studio time doing it.
Did these thoughts and checking start within 3 months after your aunt died?
I’m not really sure about the timing. I just know it started around the period when I was putting the memorial together.
How long after your aunt died did these thoughts and checking begin?
I honestly can’t say how long after. It was around the time I started working on the memorial, but I don’t remember a clear point when the thoughts and checking began.
Since your aunt died, have you often felt a strong sense that life is empty or meaningless without her?
No, I haven’t really felt that life is empty or meaningless without her.
Do you think these thoughts and checking would still be happening if your aunt had not died?

I think I probably would still be doing it. I’ll reread the label text, nudge the same objects on the table, and check the layout photos over and over until it feels settled, even though I know it’s already fine and I’m losing studio time.
